contexts.text: The foundations of the earth do shake ().
The earth hath quaked before Him ().
If they only think from a certain interior commotion...
I will commove the heaven, and the earth shall be commoved out of its place ()... The earth is said to be commoved out of its place when the Church is changed as to state.
Is this the man commoving the earth, commoving kingdoms? ()... The earth = the Church, which he is said to commove, when he claims for himself all things of it.

The powers of the heavens shall be shaken () = the foundations of the Church, which are said to be shaken when they perish. For the Church on earth is the foundation of Heaven... and therefore when the man of the Church is in so perverted a state that he no longer admits the influx of good and truth, the powers of the heavens are said to be shaken.
(Joseph's) compassions were commoved () = mercy from love.
To be in consternation = commotion; consternation is nothing else. By commotion is meant a new disposition and ordination of truths in the Natural. Explained.
The commotion of all things at the presence of the Divine. Signified.
The whole mountain trembled exceedingly = the commotion [of Heaven]... That there is commotion at the presence of the Divine. See above.
The people saw and were commoved () = the tremor which there is when Divine truths are being received.
By to move the water, here, () was signified vivification through acknowledgement and faith; thus also purification through truths. Motion = a state of life.
That it shall not be moved () = that it cannot be weakened and destroyed.
Concerning a certain Gentile who was commoved from the Word.
He was so commoved thereby that his commotion from the internal was perceived...

The earth = the Church, which is said to be commoved, and to tremble () when it is perverted by truths being falsified; and then the foundations of the mountains are said to tremble, and to commove themselves (); for the goods of love, which are founded upon the truths of faith, vanish.
The change and perversion of the Church is signified by that the earth hath quaked, and the heavens have trembled ().
To be commoved in the viscera () = mercy and charity from the interior.

By to be changed, to be commoved, to be thrown into a tumult, to be disturbed, and to tremble () is signified the state of truths when they are perishing, and in their place there enter falsities and evils; consequently the state of the Church when it is being vastated as to goods and being desolated as to truths.
The rest became terrified = commotion of the lower mind, and the conversion of those who had been a little spiritual.
To commove the earth, to make kingdoms tremble () = to destroy all things of the Church.
At this day the Quakers have not the tremor and total shaking, as before; but an uncertain shaking at the left side of the body and face.
